what: James Hardie makes fibre cement building products: exterior cladding, backer board and trim used on houses, mostly in North America. It acquired the US outdoor living company AZEK.
customers: Housebuilders, remodelling contractors and building products distributors, mostly in the United States.
moat: Fibre cement that is sold as a replacement for wood and vinyl on durability grounds, with a brand that contractors specify by name and manufacturing few can match at scale.
risks: US housing starts and remodelling have been weak with high mortgage rates
Debt of about $4.1 billion from the AZEK acquisition
Net margin fell to about 2% after acquisition charges
opportunities: Revenue grew about 25% last year as AZEK was consolidated
Analysts see about 25% upside from current levels
Fibre cement keeps taking share from wood and vinyl cladding
watch: North American volume growth and AZEK integration synergies.
